figure: FIGURE 8.2 — Per-GPU roofline: dense FP16, one H100 vs one H200
issue: The prefill operating point is labelled with an arithmetic intensity of '9.2K FLOP/byte', which is ~1000× too large, and the marker appears to be plotted near x ≈ 10^4 rather than between 10^0 and 10^1. The label conflates the token count (9.2K tokens) with the intensity value. The caption gives an intensity for the decode-batch-8 point (8 FLOP/byte) but none for prefill, so the caption does not repair the figure.
evidence: Rendered page 145 (PDF 165): orange annotation reads 'prefill 9.2K / intensity = 9.2K / FLOP/byte'; the orange marker sits on the compute plateau at an x-position near the right edge of the plot (≈10^4), to the right of both ridge lines (206 and 295). Independent recomputation from the book's own canonical inputs: prefill FLOPs = 2 × 70e9 params × 9200 tokens = 1.288e15 FLOP; bytes ≈ 140 GB weights + 24.9 GB KV ≈ 165 GB → 7.8 FLOP/byte; weight-only (the basis the figure uses for decode, where intensity = B) → 1.288e15 / 140e9 = 9.2 FLOP/byte. The correct value is therefore ≈9.2 FLOP/byte, not 9.2K. The figure's own decode labels ('decode batch B=8 (intensity = B FLOP/byte)') confirm the weight-only convention, under which prefill intensity = 9.2.
acceptance_test: The prefill annotation must read 'prefill 9.2K tokens: intensity ≈ 9.2 FLOP/byte (weight-only)' and the marker must be plotted at x = 9.2 (between the 10^0 and 10^1 ticks, i.e. left of both ridge lines) on the compute plateau. The caption must state the prefill intensity explicitly (≈9.2 FLOP/byte) so the figure and caption agree.

figure: Figure 22.1 (cited on this page as support for the attention-term share of prefill FLOPs)
issue: The bullet 'Attention / memory constrained (within prefill)' cites Fig 22.1 and gives the attention term as '4*n_layers*L*4', which as rendered is not a recognizable attention-FLOP expression (the standard form is 4*n_layers*L^2*d_model). The accompanying claim 'at 32K it is already ~60%' is workload- and model-dependent and must be checked against the canonical model's layer count and hidden size: with n_layers = 80 and d_model = 8192, attention FLOPs at 32K are 4*80*32768^2*8192 = 2.68 PFLOP against 4.48 PFLOP of linear work, i.e. ~37%, not ~60% (60% is reached near ~80K). The claim may still be correct if the canonical model differs, but as printed it is unsupported by the formula shown and by the cited figure.
evidence: p.172: 'at 128K contexts this term dominates prefill cost (at 32K it is already ~60% - the 4*n_layers*L*4 term, Fig 22.1)'. Recomputation with the canonical 70B reference (n_layers = 80, d_model = 8192): attention = 4*80*L^2*8192; at L = 32,000 -> 2.68 PFLOP; linear = 2*70e9*32,000 = 4.48 PFLOP; share = 37.5%. Share reaches 60% at L ~ 80,000.
acceptance_test: Verify the canonical model's n_layers and d_model, then restate the attention FLOP expression in a self-consistent form (4*n_layers*L^2*d_model) and recompute the 32K share; if it is not ~60%, correct the number or restate it as 'at 32K it is already ~X%'. Confirm that Fig 22.1 plots the same quantity at the same operating point, and that the page's own footnote arithmetic (2*70B*L -> 0.28 PFLOP at 2K, ~4.5 PFLOP at 32K, ~1.29 PFLOP at 9.2K) is reproduced in Fig 22.1.

figure: Figure 9.1 (forward reference from prose)
issue: The prose paragraph that introduces the ring model quotes one-way 140 GB times (0.31 s NVLink, 5.6 s HDR, 56 s Ethernet) without stating the 1.75x ring factor that Fig 9.1 applies, so the reader meets two different sets of times for '140 GB' before reaching the figure. Fig 9.1 (p.178) plots 544 ms / 6,125 ms / 98,000 ms at the same 140 GB logical tensor because it charges 1.75x the tensor per rank.
acceptance_test: The p.157 paragraph must add one sentence stating that a ring all-reduce moves 2*(N-1)/N = 1.75x the tensor per rank at N = 8, so Fig 9.1's times are 1.75x the one-way times quoted here, and must point forward to Fig 9.1 by name.
